question.problem:
Consider the function $y=({x}^{4}+1){3}^{x+4}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}={3}^{x+4}\cdot (a{x}^{4}+b{x}^{3}+c).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=({x}^{4}+1){3}^{x+4}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{4}+1){3}^{x+4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+1)+(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+1)+(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{{x}^{4}+1}\cdot 4{x}^{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=({x}^{4}+1){3}^{x+4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =({x}^{4}+1){3}^{x+4}(\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)) \\  & ={3}^{x+4}(4{x}^{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)({x}^{4}+1)) \\  & ={3}^{x+4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3){x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3))\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
a+b+c=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+4+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)=4+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).
$$
